Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Household, washing & chores

cover noun and verb

also covering, cover up, cover up (against the cold), take cover, under cover of darkness

classical

Cic. ND 2.150: tegumenta corporum vel texta vel sūta (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 298

tegumentum (tegimentum), tegumentī n.

noun, second declension

a cover, covering

Other words

  • operiō, operīre, operuī, opertum — cover, cover up

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 298

  • tegō, tegere, tēxī, tēctum — cover; roof over; hide

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.143: amīca corpus ejus tēxit suō palliō (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 6.30: fugientem silvae tēxērunt (Lewis & Short)

    The verb of tēctum, a roof, and tegumentum, a covering.

Examples

  • suffugere

    to take coverTraupman 298

  • nocte adjuvante

    under cover of darknessTraupman 298

  • amīca corpus ejus tēxit suō palliō

    his mistress covered his body with her own cloakCic. Div. 2.143 (Lewis & Short)

  • fugientem silvae tēxērunt

    the woods hid him as he fledCaes. BG 6.30 (Lewis & Short)

See also lid, shelter, blanket, hide.
